name: Beef Liver
description: Beef liver is widely regarded as the ultimate king of superfoods. It contains an unmatched, highly concentrated matrix of pre-formed vitamins, essential minerals, and complete proteins, making it drastically superior to standard muscle meats in nutritional value.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Provides nutrient-dense energy with a very low caloric cost relative to its massive vitamin profile.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: An exceptionally rich source of highly bioavailable, complete protein containing all essential amino acids for tissue synthesis.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Low in total lipids, featuring a balanced profile of monounsaturated, polyunsaturated, and essential saturated fatty acids.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Sourced naturally from stored animal glycogen. It represents a rare carbohydrate presence in meat, keeping a low glycemic index.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A (Retinol)
microNutrients.description: Pre-formed active Vitamin A (retinol) that directly fuels the visual cycle, maintains endothelial integrity, and fortifies systemic immunity.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B12
microNutrients.description: An astronomical concentration essential for myelin sheath repair, DNA replication, and preventing megaloblastic anemia.

microNutrients.name: Copper
microNutrients.description: Acts as a vital biochemical catalyst for iron metabolism, collagen structure synthesis, and defense against oxidative stress.

microNutrients.name: Iron (Heme)
microNutrients.description: Highly absorbable heme iron that binds instantly to hemoglobin, optimizing cellular oxygen transport and preventing fatigue.

microNutrients.name: Fate (Vitamin B9)
microNutrients.description: Critical for cellular division, rapid amino acid conversion, and optimizing prenatal neural tube development.

microNutrients.name: Choline
microNutrients.description: A foundational building block for cell membrane phospholipids and the neurotransmitter acetylcholine, driving memory and cognitive focus.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)
microNutrients.description: Crucial for mitochondrial respiration, electron transport chains, and converting macronutrients into actual ATP energy units.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
microNutrients.description: Supports DNA repair, skin health, and plays an essential role in converting macronutrients into cellular energy.

microNutrients.name: Zinc
microNutrients.description: Vital for immune response, wound healing, testosterone synthesis, and robust metabolic health.

microNutrients.name: Selenium
microNutrients.description: Provides powerful antioxidant defense, guarding tissues against oxidative stress and supporting thyroid hormone function.

healthBenefits: Unrivaled Anemia Prevention: The combination of high-density heme iron, copper, and vitamin B12 provides all necessary structural raw materials for efficient red blood cell production.
Advanced Cognitive Architecture: Tremendous concentrations of B-vitamins paired with Choline maximize neurotransmitter generation, preserving rapid brain signaling and nervous system integrity.
Enhanced Metabolic Performance: Acts as a powerful coenzyme powerhouse; its extreme riboflavin and pantothenic acid values catalyze the rapid breakdown of dietary elements into pure kinetic energy.

Immune & Vision Optimization: Provides massive doses of active, bioavailable retinol (Vitamin A) that directly strengthens cornea function, supports night vision, and reinforces white blood cell response.
precautions: Vitamin A Toxicity (Hypervitaminosis A): Because liver holds pre-formed Vitamin A, which is fat-soluble and stores in our tissues, eating it daily can cause toxicity. Limiting consumption to 1-2 times per week is highly advised.

Pregnancy Safety Thresholds: Expectant mothers should strictly manage liver intake. Excess pre-formed Vitamin A (retinol) carries a documented risk of causing congenital developmental defects in the fetus.

Copper Accumulation Risk: The extremely high copper content means frequent intake can over-accumulate in the body, which might lead to oxidative strain or complicate issues for individuals with underlying copper metabolic conditions.

Purine Density & Gout Management: Organ meats are naturally heavy in purine structures. These break down into uric acid, which can aggregate inside joints and trigger painful flares in individuals prone to gout.
